app.name: Shopify (Shopify Admin API app, registered in the Dev Dashboard under a Partner account)

verdict.summary: Connecting your own store is quick and needs no review: create a custom app in the Dev Dashboard, paste the client ID and secret into Composio, and install. Listing a public app requires Shopify App Review, and any request for customer name, address, email, or phone adds a data protection review.
verdict.hands_on_effort: 1-2 hours to connect your own store; 1-3 days of work to prepare a public listing (assets, webhooks, screencast, privacy policy), plus review time
verdict.time_to_first_connection: About 30-60 min once you have a Partner account and a development or own store
verdict.approval_wait: None for custom use on your own store. For public listing, Shopify publishes no review timeline; one community anecdote reports about 15 hours (not official).

gates.name: Custom app, your own store (no review)
gates.unlocks: Your own app works on a store you control. You can run the Composio OAuth flow end to end and make real Admin API calls.
limits: Custom distribution is chosen in the Dev Dashboard; the distribution method cannot be changed once selected (community source, confirm against current Shopify docs)
Custom apps cannot use the Billing API to charge merchants
gates.time_to_reach: 30-60 min after a Partner account exists

gates.name: Invited and test stores (custom install links)
gates.unlocks: Your custom app can be installed on development stores and, for Plus customers, on several stores in one organization through an install link generated from the Partner Dashboard. Protected customer data can be used in development on development stores.
limits: Protected customer data needs a distribution method selected first, even for development-store-only use (f20)
Development-store use of protected customer data needs no review once fields are selected
Install caps and user counts for custom apps were not found in the sources (see open questions)
gates.time_to_reach: Same day as Gate 1, once a distribution method is selected

gates.name: Public App Store listing (Shopify App Review)
gates.unlocks: Any merchant can install the app from the Shopify App Store after review.
limits: Compliance webhooks must be subscribed before submission
New public apps must use the GraphQL Admin API only
Protected customer data (Level 1 and Level 2) requires review for public apps
Reviewers may reject at their discretion; repeated failed exchanges can trigger a cooldown
Test credentials with full feature access and a demo screencast are required
gates.time_to_reach: Unknown. No official timeline; one community anecdote of about 15 hours (not official).

steps.title: Decide custom or public distribution before you build
steps.detail: Choose custom distribution if the app will only run on your own stores or a client's stores. Choose public only if you plan to list it in the App Store, because that path brings listing and review requirements. Shopify says the choice cannot be changed later, so confirm this in current Shopify docs before you select.
gotchas: A community blog says a client-built app selected as public can be locked into public review; verify before selecting.
Public apps need the GraphQL Admin API only and cannot charge via the Billing API if they are custom.

steps.title: Create the app in the Dev Dashboard
steps.detail: Sign in at partners.shopify.com with your Partner account. Create a new app in the Dev Dashboard (the Help Center path for custom apps is Settings, then Apps, then Develop apps, then Build apps in Dev Dashboard, then Create app). Name the app; a name is required and capped at 30 characters if you list publicly.
gotchas: Since January 1, 2026, new custom apps are built in the Dev Dashboard and then installed on a store; the old admin route is closed for new apps (community source).
The creation steps come from Help Center and community posts, not a direct walkthrough of the public-app flow.

steps.title: Register the redirect URI
steps.detail: In the app's configuration, add the redirect URL. It must match exactly, so copy it from Composio rather than typing it. If you manage the app with the Shopify CLI, add the same URL to the [auth] section of shopify.app.toml instead.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: Composio's OAUTH2 default is https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add. Use the URL shown in your Composio auth config, and make sure it is registered here.
The redirect_uri in the authorize request must match a configured value exactly, including the path and any trailing slash.

steps.title: Copy the client ID and secret into Composio
steps.detail: Copy the Client ID and Client secret from the app's settings in the Dev Dashboard. In Composio, create an OAUTH2 auth config for the shopify toolkit and paste both values in. Composio has no managed OAuth app for Shopify, so this step is required.
gotchas: Keep the client secret out of shared docs and screenshots.
Composio lists an S2S_OAUTH2 config too, but I did not verify it. It may only apply to stores in the app's own organization.

steps.title: Trim the scope list to what you use
steps.detail: The Composio default list has about 36 read/write scopes. Draft a shorter list that covers only the endpoints your agent calls, and write one line of justification per scope. Remember that a write scope also grants its matching read scope, so you do not need to list both.
gotchas: Public apps may be asked to prove each scope is needed; read_all_orders, write_payment_mandate and read_advanced_dom_pixel_events need stated justification.
Scopes that unlock protected customer data add review requirements beyond the scope request.

steps.title: Install the app on your own store and run the OAuth flow
steps.detail: Install the app on a store you control from the Dev Dashboard. The authorize request goes to https://{subdomain}.myshopify.com/admin/oauth/authorize with a comma-separated scope list, your redirect_uri, and a unique state nonce. Accept the permissions, then confirm the callback arrives.
gotchas: Replace {subdomain} with the store's myshopify subdomain for each store.
Public apps may not ask the merchant to type a myshopify.com domain during install.

steps.title: Verify the HMAC and exchange the code
steps.detail: On callback, recompute an HMAC-SHA256 over the query parameters using the client secret and compare it to the hmac value. If they match, exchange the code at the access_token endpoint. The official sample requests expiring offline tokens with expiring=1, which returns a refresh token and expires_in; refresh with grant_type=refresh_token.
gotchas: The access-token expiry and refresh-token lifetime are not stated on the pages I read; the only hint is a one-hour retry window in code comments. Do not hard-code a lifetime.
Run the refresh path in testing, not only the first exchange.

steps.title: Run a test authorization through Composio
steps.detail: Connect a test account through Composio using your OAUTH2 auth config. Make one read call and one write call against your store to confirm the scopes work. Keep the test store and the call log for your records.

steps.title: Decide whether you need protected customer data
steps.detail: Only request protected customer data if your app needs name, address, email, or phone. Level 1 excludes those fields; Level 2 includes them. Request access from the app's API access requests page and select the fields one at a time. The distribution method must be selected first.
gotchas: Development-store use needs no review once the fields are selected.
Public apps need review for both levels, and reviews focus on apps with many installs, many customer records, many approved fields, or long retention.

steps.title: Install on test or client stores through an install link
steps.detail: For more than one store, generate an install link from the Partner Dashboard and send it to invited users or the client. For Plus customers, one link can install the app on several stores in the same organization. Repeat the OAuth test on each store.
gotchas: Install caps and user limits for unlisted custom apps were not found; check Partner Dashboard limits before promising access to many stores.

steps.title: Check public-app technical requirements
steps.detail: Only if you plan a public listing: confirm the app uses the GraphQL Admin API exclusively, runs OAuth before any other step after install, sends the merchant to the app UI after permissions are accepted, and serves a valid TLS/SSL certificate. Reinstalls must also run OAuth first.
gotchas: Expired or invalid certificates and 404 or 500 pages are grounds for rejection.

steps.title: Subscribe to compliance webhooks
steps.detail: Draft the compliance webhook subscriptions required for public apps and add them to the app configuration. You verify that they are subscribed before submission.
gotchas: This is required before you submit a public app for review.

steps.title: Prepare listing assets and contacts
steps.detail: Prepare a 1200 x 1200 pixel app icon in JPEG or PNG, your privacy policy URL, configured app URLs, an emergency developer contact with email and phone, and an API contact email. The API contact email must not contain the word Shopify. Lead the app name with your own brand.

steps.title: Record a demo screencast and set up test credentials
steps.detail: Record a screencast of setup and features as the listing describes them. Create test credentials that give the reviewer full access to the app's features. A community write-up says the pre-listing review also checks functionality, Lighthouse performance, listing accuracy, and browser compatibility; verify this in current docs.
gotchas: Recording the video and creating credentials are manual steps; an agent can draft the script.

steps.title: Submit for App Store review and handle the response
steps.detail: Submit the app for review from the Dev Dashboard once every item above is done. Answer review emails quickly. Shopify can reject at its discretion, and repeated failed exchanges or slow replies can trigger a cooldown that blocks resubmission.
gotchas: The cooldown affects only the app under review and lengthens on repeat.
No official review timeline was found; plan for an unknown wait.

requirements.item: Distribution method selected in the Dev Dashboard
requirements.detail: Required before anything else, including protected customer data requests. Cannot be changed after selection per Shopify (community source says confirm).
Must match the Composio callback URL exactly, in the Dev Dashboard or shopify.app.toml [auth] section.

requirements.item: Custom apps cannot charge merchants via Billing API
requirements.detail: Any paid model requires a public app.

requirements.item: Protected customer data review for public apps
requirements.detail: Public apps need review for Level 1 and Level 2 protected customer data. Custom apps have them without review.
Encrypted backups, test and production data separation, DLP strategy, limited staff access, strong staff passwords, access log, and a written security incident response policy.
Required for App Store distribution before submission.
New public apps must use GraphQL exclusively since April 1, 2025.

requirements.item: OAuth before anything else; valid TLS
requirements.detail: Authenticate with OAuth immediately after install and on reinstall; hosting needs an error-free TLS certificate.

requirements.item: Icon, privacy policy, contacts, screencast, test credentials
requirements.detail: 1200 x 1200 icon; privacy policy; emergency contact email and phone; API contact email without the word Shopify; demo screencast; test credentials with full feature access.

scopes.effect: The Composio default list is broad. Trim it to the scopes your agent actually calls. A write scope also grants its read scope, so list only the write scope where both are needed.
Public apps must justify this scope in the listing; reviewers can ask for proof it is needed.
Requires a stated justification for public apps.
Requires a stated justification for public apps.

scopes.scope: Protected customer data scopes (name, address, email, phone fields)
scopes.effect: Adds the protected customer data request. Usable in development on development stores without review; public apps need a data protection review.

blockers.symptom: Public listing stalls or is rejected at review
blockers.cause: Shopify's App Review team can reject at its discretion, and missing requirements or 404/500 errors are listed as unacceptable.
blockers.fix: Work through the Gate 3 checklist before submitting. Keep hosting error-free and respond to review emails promptly to avoid a cooldown.

blockers.symptom: Protected customer data request needs review and the listing is delayed
blockers.cause: Public apps must pass data protection review for Level 1 and Level 2 fields, and Level 2 adds security requirements.
blockers.fix: Request only the fields you need. If you can avoid name, address, email, and phone, skip Level 2 and the associated security requirements.

blockers.symptom: Distribution choice cannot be changed after you pick public or custom
blockers.cause: Shopify says the distribution method cannot be changed after selection; a community source says a client-built app selected as public can be locked into review.
blockers.fix: Confirm the rule in current Shopify docs before selecting. If you only need your own or client stores, choose custom.

blockers.symptom: Merchant install fails because it asks for a myshopify.com domain
blockers.cause: Public apps must not request manual entry of a myshopify.com URL during install.
blockers.fix: Start installs from Shopify-owned surfaces such as the App Store or an install link.

blockers.symptom: Redirect fails with a mismatched redirect_uri
blockers.cause: The redirect_uri in the authorize request must exactly match a configured value, and the Composio default is a specific URL.
blockers.fix: Copy the callback URL from the Composio auth config and register it exactly in the Dev Dashboard or shopify.app.toml.

composio.note: Composio has no managed OAuth app for Shopify. Register your own app in the Dev Dashboard and enter its client ID and secret in a Composio OAUTH2 auth config. Allow the Composio callback URL shown in that auth config as a redirect URI. The default list is broad, so trim it to the scopes you use before any public submission. Choose custom or public distribution before you build, because the choice is hard to reverse.

open_questions: No official review timeline was found. The only figure is one community anecdote of about 15 hours, which is not an official timeline.
Exact access-token expiry (expires_in) and refresh-token lifetime are not stated on the pages read. Only code comments mention a one-hour retry window. Test refresh before relying on it.
Not confirmed whether a new public app needs an organization admin, a paid Partner plan, or business verification.
The Dev Dashboard flow for creating a public app was not fetched directly; creation steps come from Help Center and community posts.
Shopify does not publish a single list of rejection reasons; the common reasons are inferred from the requirements and community write-ups.
No rate limit or install cap for unreviewed public apps was found. Shopify API rate limits, including any lower limits for new apps, were not researched.
Whether the distribution method is truly irreversible rests on Shopify's statement plus a community blog. Confirm in current docs before selecting.
Composio's S2S_OAUTH2 (client credentials) config is listed but not verified against Shopify's docs. It may only apply to stores in the app's own organization.
The authorize endpoint probe returned a storefront 404 for an invalid client_id, so how Shopify validates unknown clients was not shown. A real Dev Dashboard client_id is needed for that test.

Whether protected customer data is requested in the Partner Dashboard or the Dev Dashboard: the findings name the Partner Dashboard API access requests page, but the app creation flow is in the Dev Dashboard. Confirm where the request form sits.
